Why does your own voice sound wrong on a recording?

Kevin Trudeau explains that when you play back a recording, all of the sound reaches your ear. When you speak live, only a fraction comes in through the ear. Most of it travels through the vocal cords and bone and vibrates the brain directly.

That is why the words you say out loud land so deeply. Kevin says that when you speak, you are virtually speaking things into existence.

When did you last really listen to how you talk about your own life?
